claims.title: Global Artin reciprocity and kernel identification with idèle-class norms
claims.hypotheses: Number fields K and L with L/K a finite abelian Galois extension, idèle group 𝕀_K with diagonal embedding diag : K^× ↪ 𝕀_K and idèle class group C_K = 𝕀_K / K^×, local Artin norm residue symbols assembling into the continuous surjective global idèle symbol θ_{L/K} : 𝕀_K → Gal(L/K) with arithmetic Frobenius normalization, and the cyclic class-field axiom (|Ĥ⁰(G, C_L)| = [L : K], |Ĥ⁻¹(G, C_L)| = 1) from HNT-01 supplying the abstract class-formation reciprocity map on finite subfields of ℚ̄.
claims.statement: The global idèle symbol θ_{L/K} : 𝕀_K → Gal(L/K) satisfies the global product formula θ_{L/K}(diag(a)) = 1 for every a ∈ K^× and has kernel ker(θ_{L/K}) = diag(K^×) · N_{L/K}(𝕀_L). Consequently θ_{L/K} descends to a continuous surjective global Artin reciprocity homomorphism θ̄_{L/K} : C_K → Gal(L/K) with kernel ker(θ̄_{L/K}) = N_{L/K}(C_L), inducing a group isomorphism C_K / N_{L/K}(C_L) ≅ Gal(L/K) and the abelian norm-index equality [C_K : N_{L/K}(C_L)] = [L : K].
definitions: global idèle symbol θ_{L/K} : 𝕀_K → Gal(L/K) defined as the product over all finite and infinite places of local norm residue symbols
global Artin reciprocity homomorphism θ̄_{L/K} : C_K → Gal(L/K) factoring θ_{L/K} through C_K = 𝕀_K / diag(K^×)
idèle-class norm subgroup N_{L/K}(C_L) ≤ C_K and its quotient isomorphism C_K / N_{L/K}(C_L) ≅ Gal(L/K)

Identification of abstract and local-product symbols via density and open idèle norms, product formula, and kernel over finite subfields of ℚ̄
Transfer to arbitrary finite abelian extensions, global Artin reciprocity map, continuity, and kernel identification ker = N_{L/K}(C_L)
Idèle-class norm index equality [C_K : N_{L/K}(C_L)] = [L : K] for abelian extensions

claims.correspondence: Over ℚ, checking local symbols at ∞, p, and q ≠ p shows that θ_{L/ℚ}(diag(−1)) and θ_{L/ℚ}(diag(q)) fix every p^n-th root of unity; generator induction on ℚ^× and coprime induction give the product formula for every cyclotomic extension of ℚ. For finite abelian extensions K ⊆ L inside ℚ̄, the concrete idèle symbol and the abstract class-formation reciprocity map agree on single-place embeddings and vanish on the open subgroup N_{L/K}(𝕀_L), hence agree everywhere on 𝕀_K by density, giving θ_{L/K}(diag(a)) = 1 and ker = N_{L/K}(C_L). Embedding arbitrary K ⊆ L into ℚ̄ transfers both identities, yielding the continuous surjective reciprocity homomorphism with kernel N_{L/K}(C_L) and norm index [L : K].

claims.title: Global existence theorem for abelian extensions from Kummer theory and norm limitation
claims.hypotheses: A number field K with fixed algebraic closure Ω, idèle class group C_K = 𝕀_K / K^×, and global Artin reciprocity CFT-01; for norm limitation, any finite Galois extension M/K with maximal abelian subextension M^{ab} = M^{[Gal(M/K), Gal(M/K)]}; for Kummer realization, an integer n ≥ 1 with μ_n ⊆ K and an open subgroup N ≤ C_K satisfying c^n ∈ N for all c ∈ C_K; for global existence, any open subgroup N ≤ C_K of finite index.
claims.statement: (1) Norm limitation: for every finite Galois extension M/K, N_{M/K}(C_M) = N_{M^{ab}/K}(C_{M^{ab}}) and [C_K : N_{M/K}(C_M)] = |Gal(M/K)^{ab}|; consequently every finite extension L/K admits a finite abelian extension E/K with N_{E/K}(C_E) ⊆ N_{L/K}(C_L). (2) Kummer realization: if μ_n ⊆ K (n ≥ 1) and N ≤ C_K is open with C_K^n ⊆ N, then N = N_{L/K}(C_L) for a finite abelian extension L/K of exponent dividing n inside an S-unit Kummer extension. (3) Global existence and order-reversing correspondence: every finite abelian extension L/K has an open finite-index norm subgroup N_{L/K}(C_L) ≤ C_K, every open finite-index subgroup N ≤ C_K equals N_{L/K}(C_L) for a unique finite abelian intermediate field L ⊆ Ω, and L₁ ⊆ L₂ holds if and only if N_{L₂/K}(C_{L₂}) ⊆ N_{L₁/K}(C_{L₁}).
definitions: maximal abelian subextension M^{ab} fixed by the commutator subgroup [Gal(M/K), Gal(M/K)]
S-unit Kummer extension K(𝒪_{K,S}^{× 1/n}) and its idèle-class norm subgroup generated by local n-th powers at S and ∞
order-reversing correspondence L ↦ N_{L/K}(C_L) between finite abelian subfields of Ω over K and open finite-index subgroups of C_K

sources.label: Norm limitation theorem N_{M/K}(C_M) = N_{M^{ab}/K}(C_{M^{ab}}) and abelian norm subgroup inside any finite extension
Galois fixed-field realization, power-subgroup containment, and Kummer realization when μ_n ⊆ K
Cyclotomic base change removing μ_n, global existence in Ω, openness of norm groups, and inclusion-reversing bijection

claims.correspondence: Abstract reciprocity on Gal(M/K)^{ab} makes [C_K : N_{M/K}(C_M)] divide |Gal(M/K)^{ab}| = [C_K : N_{M^{ab}/K}(C_{M^{ab}})]; together with norm transitivity N_{M/K}(C_M) ⊆ N_{M^{ab}/K}(C_{M^{ab}}), divisibility antisymmetry proves norm limitation. When μ_n ⊆ K, openness of N gives a congruence subgroup U(𝔪) inside N and class-group finiteness enlarges its support to S so that the S-unit Kummer extension has norm group ≤ N; taking the fixed field of θ̄(N) yields norm group equal to N. For an arbitrary open subgroup N of finite index m, passing to K' = K(μ_m) pulls N back to N' with C_{K'}^m ⊆ N', Kummer realization gives L'/K' with N_{L'/K}(C_{L'}) ⊆ N, norm limitation produces an abelian E/K with N_{E/K}(C_E) ⊆ N, and Galois theory inside E gives L with N_{L/K}(C_L) = N; composita and reciprocity establish the order-reversing correspondence.
claims.review: Verified that Kummer.lean:178 still assumes μ_n ⊆ K while cyclotomic base change K' = K(μ_m) occurs in ExistsIsAbelianGaloisRangeIdeleClassNormEqOfFini.lean:103–125; checked range [35, 185] strictly disjoint from ART-01's [209, 225]; verified cubic example E ⊂ ℚ(ζ_7) via K' = ℚ(μ_3).

claims.title: Ray class fields, prime splitting laws, and Hilbert unramified reciprocity
claims.hypotheses: A number field K with fixed algebraic closure Ω, a modulus 𝔪 = (𝔪_0, 𝔪_∞) consisting of a nonzero integral ideal 𝔪_0 ⊆ 𝒪_K and a set 𝔪_∞ of real infinite places of K, global Artin reciprocity CFT-01, and the global existence correspondence CFT-02.
claims.statement: (1) Idèlic-to-ideal ray class isomorphism: weak approximation and the fractional-ideal valuation map identify the idèlic ray class group C_K / [U(𝔪)] with the finite ideal ray class group Cl_𝔪(K) = I(𝔪) / P_𝔪. (2) Ray class field, unramifiedness, and splitting law: the unique finite abelian extension K(𝔪) ⊆ Ω with N_{K(𝔪)/K}(C_{K(𝔪)}) = [U(𝔪)] satisfies Cl_𝔪(K) ≅ Gal(K(𝔪)/K) via the Artin map sending [𝔭] to arithmetic Frobenius Frob_𝔭 for every finite prime 𝔭 ∤ 𝔪_0; every such prime 𝔭 is unramified in K(𝔪)/K and splits completely in K(𝔪) if and only if Frob_𝔭 = 1, equivalently [𝔭] = 1 in Cl_𝔪(K). Moreover, every finite abelian extension L ⊆ Ω over K lies inside some ray class field K(𝔪). (3) Everywhere-unramified extensions and Hilbert class field: for any finite abelian extension L/K unramified at all finite and infinite places, the global idèle symbol vanishes on all finite-unit idèles (with arbitrary infinite components), placing [U(1)] ⊆ N_{L/K}(C_L) and hence L ⊆ H = K(1) for the trivial modulus 𝔪 = (1, ∅).
definitions: modulus 𝔪 = (𝔪_0, 𝔪_∞), ray congruence subgroup U(𝔪) ≤ 𝕀_K, coprime fractional ideals I(𝔪), and ray principal ideals P_𝔪
ray class field K(𝔪) ⊆ Ω cut out by [U(𝔪)] ≤ C_K and its Artin isomorphism Cl_𝔪(K) ≅ Gal(K(𝔪)/K)
everywhere-unramified extension (e(w/v) = 1 at every finite place and no real place becomes complex) and trivial modulus 𝔪 = (1, ∅)

claims.correspondence: Weak approximation onto finite places dividing 𝔪_0 and real places in 𝔪_∞ shows that 𝕀_K(𝔪) surjects onto C_K/[U(𝔪)] and onto Cl_𝔪(K) with the same kernel 𝕀_K(𝔪) ∩ (diag(K^×) · U(𝔪)), giving C_K/[U(𝔪)] ≅ Cl_𝔪(K). Composing with reciprocity for K(𝔪) gives the Artin isomorphism Cl_𝔪(K) ≅ Gal(K(𝔪)/K). Outside 𝔪_0, local units lie in U(𝔪), so local symbols vanish on units; local uniformizer counting yields e = 1, reducing complete splitting to Frob_𝔭 = 1 and hence [𝔭] = 1 in Cl_𝔪(K). For everywhere-unramified abelian extensions, local finite unit symbols and infinite symbols both vanish, forcing θ_{L/K} = 1 on all finite-unit idèles and embedding L into the Hilbert class field K(1).
